scenarioName: Pedestrian vs. Auto — Multi-System Trauma with Flail Chest

scenarioStory.history: Bystanders report the patient was crossing an intersection when she was struck by a sedan traveling an estimated 40 mph; she was thrown approximately 15 feet and landed on the pavement. On arrival she is awake, in severe distress, complaining of chest and left flank pain, with visibly paradoxical movement of the left lateral chest wall with each breath. Denies loss of consciousness per bystanders, though she is disoriented to time.
scenarioStory.course: Initial Contact: Crew arrives to find a 52-year-old female pedestrian struck by a vehicle at high speed, thrown approximately 15 feet. She is alert but tachypneic and in severe pain, with visible paradoxical movement of the left chest wall consistent with a flail segment. → Primary survey and SMR completed: Crew completes the MARCH primary survey, applies high-flow oxygen for hypoxia, palpates the chest wall confirming flail segment without tracheal deviation or absent breath sounds, and initiates cervical collar and spinal motion restriction given the severe distracting injuries. → Fluid bolus and fentanyl given: Crew initiates a 500 mL crystalloid bolus for persistent tachycardia and administers weight-based fentanyl for severe pain, reassessing vitals and pain score after each intervention. → Reassessed and prepared for transport: Patient is packaged with spinal motion restriction, splinted leg, oxygen, and IV access, and transported with continued serial reassessment given the multi-system mechanism.

patientInformation.patientCondition: Struck by vehicle, severe chest and body pain

scenarioEvents.name: Initial Contact
scenarioEvents.description: Crew arrives to find a 52-year-old female pedestrian struck by a vehicle at high speed, thrown approximately 15 feet. She is alert but tachypneic and in severe pain, with visible paradoxical movement of the left chest wall consistent with a flail segment.

scenarioEvents.name: Primary survey and SMR completed
scenarioEvents.description: Crew completes the MARCH primary survey, applies high-flow oxygen for hypoxia, palpates the chest wall confirming flail segment without tracheal deviation or absent breath sounds, and initiates cervical collar and spinal motion restriction given the severe distracting injuries.
relatedChecklist: Perform MARCH primary survey: hemorrhage, airway, breathing, circulation, head/hypothermia
Palpate chest wall for instability/crepitus; auscultate breath sounds bilaterally
Apply high-flow supplemental oxygen to target SpO2 greater than 94%
Apply cervical collar and initiate spinal motion restriction for distracting injuries

scenarioEvents.name: Fluid bolus and fentanyl given
scenarioEvents.description: Crew initiates a 500 mL crystalloid bolus for persistent tachycardia and administers weight-based fentanyl for severe pain, reassessing vitals and pain score after each intervention.
relatedChecklist: 500 mL crystalloid IV bolus for HR >120 bpm; reassess and repeat as needed
Fentanyl 70 mcg IV (70 kg × 1 mcg/kg; max initial dose 100 mcg)

scenarioEvents.name: Reassessed and prepared for transport
scenarioEvents.description: Patient is packaged with spinal motion restriction, splinted leg, oxygen, and IV access, and transported with continued serial reassessment given the multi-system mechanism.
relatedChecklist: Reassess vital signs and breath sounds serially en route; monitor for delayed tension pneumothorax
Transport to appropriate trauma center per field triage guideline; minimize scene time

scenarioEvents.name: Chest reassessment skipped
scenarioEvents.description: Without ongoing chest reassessment, an evolving tension pneumothorax on the injured side goes unrecognized. The patient rapidly decompensates with absent breath sounds, tracheal deviation, and hypotension, requiring emergent needle decompression.
relatedChecklist: Needle decompression of left chest for tension pneumothorax with hypotension and tracheal deviation
